verdict.rationale: Logseq's docs say it exports the entire graph in several open formats: EDN, JSON, Standard Markdown, OPML, Roam JSON and HTML. Community users also confirm their data lives in local markdown files they can keep in git, so leaving is straightforward. One user calls the Markdown backend non-standard and another says the newer database version no longer stores notes as markdown files. Those are caveats about native storage, not evidence that the documented export fails. Missing for 10: hands-on verification of whole-graph export fidelity, and clarity on export parity in the newer database version.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can export my entire knowledge base at any time in open formats, so leaving is as easy as arriving

citations.quote: Exports the entire graph in the following formats: **EDN**... **JSON**... **Standard Markdown**... **OPML**... **Roam JSON**... **HTML**
It supports exporting text selections, blocks, individual pages, or the entire graph with customizable options.
